about: What real machines, and the people using them, showed must change in Windstorm Repo Minions, and the version each change is due in. A lesson here is a gate, not a note: tests/test_strand.py (class Promises) refuses a version while a row due in it has no test, and refuses the version after it until the row says where it was proven on a real machine.
how_to_use: A new lesson gets a row the day it is learned: what was seen, the promise, a codon in DNA-STRAND-MASTER-PLAN.md, the version it is due in, and a tracking issue.
When it is built: put the name of its test in 'test'. The test must exist and be named in the plan next to the codon.
When it has been seen to work on a real machine: say which kind of machine, which version and when in 'proven'.

'ship_in' moves only with a reason in 'moved_why'. A row whose owner is 'person' was seen by the person the skill is for, on their own machine: its date moves only by their word, restated in 'moved_by_person'.
A row is never deleted. A promise that turns out wrong is closed by a row that says why.
A lesson that was heard and not taken goes under 'declined' with the reason, so that nothing is dropped without a word.

rows.seen: Seen by the skill's maintainers over months: private-repository runs that ended 'startup_failure' with zero jobs while the repository's own self-hosted runner was online and idle. A test on a public repository had been taken as proof that a private one would work; it did not.
rows.promise: Before installing, look tests whether GitHub creates jobs for THIS repository and names a zero-job startup_failure as an account or repository matter; setup stops there and the skill is never offered as a way around it.

rows.seen: Seen: self-hosted runners attached to public repositories, guarded only by a same-repository condition in the workflow file and by approval of outside contributors. A fork's pull request runs its own copy of the workflow file, so the condition is not a boundary. Repositories also changed visibility after their runners were set up.
rows.promise: Refuse a repository that is not private, at the tool, and hold its runners within one watch interval when it stops being private.

rows.seen: Seen: a runner's account was in the group that controls the container service, which is admin access by another name, on a machine that also held other people's files.
rows.promise: The runner user has no admin rights and is in no group that gives them.

rows.seen: Seen: a registration token written on a command line in a runbook, and runner credential files readable by a group.
rows.promise: Tokens go by standard input only; credential files are 0600 and read back after install.

rows.seen: Seen: a job on a machine shared with a live service took that service's containers down, because both used the same default project name; fixed host ports also collided.
rows.promise: look names what already lives on the computer, and setup asks the person to choose another computer or say yes in words when it serves something live.

rows.seen: Seen: a workflow that publishes on a tag push would have published by itself once its runner came back.
rows.promise: move never moves a publishing or deploying job silently; it is left as it was and named.

rows.seen: Seen: jobs that asked for a label no online runner carried waited for hours, including on open pull requests' heads, and jobs for another OS could not run anywhere.
rows.promise: Every job no owned computer can take is named and left as it was; a lint names jobs no runner can take before they wait.

rows.seen: Seen: several runners sharing one action cache gave half-unpacked actions for a week; a copied runner folder kept links into the first runner; a home folder kept between jobs changed the next job's result.
rows.promise: Each runner is a fresh copy with its own folders and work folder, never shared.

rows.seen: Seen: work folders grew to about 90 GB on a shared server; a laptop's disk went read-only under load.
rows.promise: A disk budget, cleanup after jobs, and a hold below a free-space floor before the disk fills.

rows.seen: Seen: a machine short of memory (swap in use from other programs) slowed a job past its time limit; machines ran at load far above their cores with jobs in parallel.
rows.promise: One job at a time per runner, at low priority, inside CPU and memory limits set from the survey.

rows.seen: Seen: a restart of the machine cancelled the job running on it; after restarts, runners that had been removed on the server side kept failing to come back.
rows.promise: The runner is a boot service that comes back by itself, and status names a job a restart cut and offers to run it again once.

rows.seen: Seen: a safety stop that killed runners cut a running test and left runners that needed restoring by hand; a container stop with a short default killed a runner before its own graceful stop.
rows.promise: Every stop drains first and waits for the running job; the service stop timeout is at least the runner's own.

rows.seen: Seen: 'no job running' read from a host process count was wrong for runners in containers; a runner handed back as free had to be read after the last restart.
rows.promise: Idle is said only when GitHub says not busy and no job process runs on the computer, both read.

rows.seen: Seen: runners listed online for months that had never run a job.
rows.promise: status names runners idle for 14 days or more and runners on GitHub's side that no service of ours matches.

rows.seen: Seen: artifact storage ran out for an account whose jobs ran on its own machines.
rows.promise: The skill says storage counts the same whichever computer ran the job.

rows.seen: Read in GitHub's documentation and changelog: jobs on own runners are not charged today, but a per-minute charge was announced in December 2025 and postponed with no new date.
rows.promise: The cost sentence is read from GitHub with its date, never promised; a change is told to the person.

rows.seen: Seen: a person's sessions and test work on a shared laptop held memory while another project's job ran there, and the job was cut off at its time limit.
rows.promise: look surveys memory and swap in use, and status puts load and disk kind beside a slow result.

rows.seen: Seen many times over months: restarts of machines that carry runners (planned test restarts, a system updater, a reset) cancelled the job running at that moment; the safe practice that grew up was to hold the runner, wait for its job, and hand it back only as 'online and idle', read after the restart.
rows.promise: drain --restart holds, waits for the running job, says 'safe to restart now' only then, and the hold lifts by itself after the restart once both sides read the runner online.

rows.seen: Seen: a laptop used as a runner ran hot and throttled under a job, its disk went read-only under load, and runners on a flaky home uplink lost their jobs; a person's own computer is often a laptop that sleeps, closes its lid, runs on battery and changes networks.
rows.promise: A laptop is named before setup with what it means; on battery the runners are held by default; a sleep during a job is put off where the OS allows and what cannot be put off is said; after a wake or network change the runner is seen back on both sides.
